title: Context Language Models
authors: Rulin Shao, Shannon Zejiang Shen, Junjie Oscar Yin, Yuetai Li, Minheng Wang, Hamish Ivison, Radha Poovendran, Nathan Lambert, Teng Xiao, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Luke Zettlemoyer, Pang Wei Koh
lab: University of Washington, Meta Superintelligence Labs, MIT, Trillium Labs
date: 29 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 19 October 2026)
takeaway: Handing the model its own context as a file to rewrite makes context management model behaviour that a prompt can steer and RL can train. Zero-shot it pays off with a strong model: Qwen3.6-27B on BrowseComp-Plus scores 59.4% against 53.3% for summarisation (+11.4% relative) with 21.5% fewer calculated FLOPs and ties on TerminalBench 2.1, in single runs; with a 9B model it is not the best method. After RL the clear gain is cost (38.8% fewer FLOPs): accuracy is 0.4 points above an equally trained summary harness, and the abstract's +47.6% is against CLM's own untrained start.
takeaway_note: Scoped on 26 October 2026. The database Takeaway as fetched said CLMs beat harness-side context management and cited +47.6% after RL; the 19 October rewrite still said it beats it at lower cost in zero-shot runs without limits. The paper's own evidence: one run per setting, a tie on TerminalBench 2.1, Self-Compact ahead of CLM on BrowseComp-Plus with Qwen3.5-9B (Figure 19), FLOPs calculated rather than measured, and the +47.6% measured against CLM's untrained start (Table 2). The Notion property needs the same edit.
verdict: Believe the design (the live context as a file the model edits) and the FLOPs accounting, which reproduces to the digit. Treat the size of the accuracy wins as provisional: one run per setting, CLM alone gets retries, free editing turns and budget nudges, the RL win over a trained summary harness is 0.4 points, and on the 9B model zero-shot Self-Compact beats CLM on BrowseComp-Plus.

headline.k: BrowseComp-Plus accuracy against Codex-style summarisation (59.4% against 53.3%), with 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs
after RL: CLM 42.5% against the summary harness trained with the same recipe, 42.1%; the abstract's +47.6% is against CLM's own untrained start
Suffix Cache Reuse against standard SGLang at the same accuracy (60.2%); two thirds of the reuse comes from stripped reasoning, not from CLM edits

code.title: facebookresearch/context-language-models
code.time: 25 min for the harness and the FLOPs metric
code.note: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). The CLM harness on Harbor with the BrowseComp-Plus and EdgeBench configurations, the prefix-reuse FLOPs metric, the skill-evolution loop, the RL patches for slime, and Suffix Cache Reuse for SGLang and vLLM; read at commit 4831982 (13 October 2026)

resources.n: The four diagnostic tasks of §3 with every method's skill; the same tasks are on Hugging Face as context-language-model/ContextBench.

resources.t: Suffix Cache Reuse: overview and results
resources.n: How the SGLang patch diffs a new prompt against the previous one, re-rotates relocated keys, and handles the hybrid model's linear-attention layers.
The deep-research benchmark behind the headline: 830 questions over a fixed corpus, so search results are reproducible.
The input as a REPL variable read on demand; the closest prior design, and the one the paper calls complementary (read-only live context against read-write).
The radix-tree prefix cache whose first-mismatch rule makes mid-context edits expensive, and which Suffix Cache Reuse patches.
The earlier design that lets the model edit one fixed block inside its context; CLMs open the whole context instead.
GRPO, the group-relative advantage that the CLM efficiency advantage extends.

kb.t: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale (Latent Context Language Models)
kb.n: A different paper with a similar name: an encoder squeezes the context into latent vectors before the decoder reads it (an architecture, trained on 350B tokens). CLMs change no weights to start with; the model rewrites its own text context with Bash.

kb.t: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
kb.n: Where GRPO comes from; §4.2 here broadcasts its trajectory-level advantage to every model call of an edited trajectory.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: A harness built on recursive language models, the read-only context design CLMs are compared against.

kb.t: Proactive Memory Agent: selective reminding for long-horizon agents
kb.n: Another answer to long-horizon context: a second agent decides what to remind the worker of, instead of the worker editing its own context.

kb.t: Just-in-Time Memory: Learning to Curate Task-Adaptive Memory for LLM Agents
kb.n: Learned memory curation outside the live context; the external-memory side of the distinction Appendix A draws.

kb.t: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
kb.n: The block-level KV cache that prefix caching and Suffix Cache Reuse sit on.

kb.t: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
kb.n: The thought, action, observation loop every harness here runs; CLMs add one more kind of action, editing the transcript.

topics.t: Context engineering: window budgets, caching, compaction, memory files, subagents
topics.n: The owning page: its section 4 (Compaction, forced on purpose) cites this paper among the designs that manage context inside the model and records real Claude Code compactions call by call.

topics.t: Batching, KV cache and scheduling in depth
topics.n: Why a hit is a prefix: the block-hash lookup that stops at the first miss, the rule Suffix Cache Reuse relaxes.

topics.t: SGLang: radix cache, cache-aware scheduling, large-scale serving
topics.n: The radix tree of Appendix B, and the engine the SCR patch targets.

topics.t: Beyond attention: SSMs, Mamba, linear attention, RWKV and hybrids
topics.n: Gated DeltaNet and the hybrid layout of Qwen3.6-27B (48 of 64 layers linear), which is why only 16 layers pay the per-pair attention cost.

topics.t: Performance math: FLOPs, memory, MFU, tokens per second, costing a run
topics.n: The 2 FLOPs per multiply-add accounting behind Eq. 7 to 9.

topics.t: Agent security: permissions, sandboxes, prompt injection, egress
topics.n: §6's warning: an editable context is one more place an injected instruction can persist.

topics.t: Multi-agent patterns: orchestrator-workers, handoffs, debate, when several agents help or hurt
topics.n: Subagents and swarms as several context files; EdgeBench-10 is one more case where subagents add little.

topics.t: RL for LLMs: RLHF, GRPO, RLVR
topics.n: The RL background for §4.2's stepwise GRPO and the success-gated efficiency advantage.
